experiment_description: Four-qubit superconducting-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometry experiment configured to test a tunable wave-to-particle transition under pulsed which-way measurement. The active interferometer is the Q0–Q1–Q2–Q3 plaquette of a 4×4 frequency-tunable transmon array: Q0 acts as the first beam splitter, Q1 is path 1, Q2 is path 2 and the monitored which-way site, and Q3 acts as the second beam splitter and output port. All four qubits are initially measured and post-selected in |0>. A microwave photon is generated by applying a π pulse to Q0. Q0, Q1, and Q2 are tuned by Z pulses to the common working frequency 5.82 GHz for 57 ns to split the excitation between Q1 and Q2. The arms are then decoupled by biasing Q0 to its idle frequency, keeping Q2 at 5.82 GHz, and biasing Q1 to the waiting frequency 5.83 GHz. A 100 ns dispersive readout pulse is applied to Q2’s readout resonator as the which-way measurement, followed by a 100 ns resonator-decay wait. The calibrated average measurement-induced dephasing strength Γm/2π is swept from 0 to 3.695 MHz. A controllable phase is applied on path 1 by biasing Q1 to 5.83 GHz + δ/2π for tp = 100 ns, with δ/2π swept from 0 to 30 MHz so that the phase is phi = -tp δ. Q1, Q2, and Q3 are then tuned to 5.82 GHz for 49 ns to recombine the two paths at Q3. The Q3 excited-state population PI is measured as a function of δ and fit to a sinusoidal interference fringe. Visibility is defined as V = (PImax - PImin)/(PImax + PImin), where PImax and PImin are the fitted maximum and minimum Q3 populations over the δ sweep. The geometric scope is the entire four-qubit interferometer plaquette; the measurement compares the same output port Q3 across the full phase sweep for each calibrated Γm.

experiment_description: Two-qubit quantum-state tomography experiment on the two arms of the 4-qubit superconducting-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometer, configured to quantify how pulsed which-way measurement transfers information from the path qubits to the measurement apparatus. The active interferometer region is the same Q0–Q1–Q2–Q3 plaquette, with Q1 and Q2 representing the two arms after the first beam splitter. The preparation and first beamsplitting stage are identical to the 4-qubit interference experiment: all qubits are initially read out and post-selected in |0>, Q0 is excited by a π pulse, and Q0, Q1, and Q2 are tuned to 5.82 GHz for 57 ns. The qubits are then decoupled, and a 100 ns dispersive which-way readout pulse with calibrated average dephasing Γm is applied to Q2’s readout resonator. The Γm/2π sweep covers 0 to 3.695 MHz. Instead of applying the phase-scan and recombination steps, the circuit waits with Q1 and Q2 decoupled and then performs two-qubit tomography on Q1 and Q2. From the reconstructed density matrix rho_Q1Q2, the concurrence is computed using the Wootters definition C = max(0, λ1 - λ2 - λ3 - λ4), where λi are the square roots of the eigenvalues of rho rho_tilde in decreasing order and rho_tilde = (sigma_y ⊗ sigma_y) rho* (sigma_y ⊗ sigma_y). The single-excitation density matrix is rho_s = P rho_Q1Q2 P / Tr(P rho_Q1Q2), with P = |10><10| + |01><01|. The purity is Ps = Tr(rho_s^2), and the von Neumann entropy is Ss = -Tr(rho_s log2 rho_s). The spatial-geometric scope is the two arm qubits Q1 and Q2, measured jointly after the controlled path-splitting and which-way pulse.

experiment_description: Twelve-qubit superconducting-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometry experiment configured to test continuous which-way monitoring and quantum-Zeno backaction during coherent propagation. The active interferometer is embedded in the 4×4 transmon processor and uses 12 qubits. Q0 is the initial beam splitter; path 1 is Q1, Q4, Q5, Q7, and Q13; path 2 is Q2, Q8, Q10, Q11, and Q14; Q15 is the final beam splitter/output region. All participating qubits are initially biased to idle frequencies and measured for initial-state post-selection. A microwave photon is generated by exciting Q0. The 12 interferometer qubits are then tuned to the common working frequency 5.82 GHz for coherent evolution over a time window from 0 to 200 ns. The central mechanism tested is that continuous dispersive monitoring of Q2, a site at the entrance to path 2, can both provide which-way information and alter transport by quantum-Zeno reflection when the measurement-induced dephasing rate becomes comparable to or exceeds the Q0–Q2 hopping scale. The which-way measurement pulse on Q2’s readout resonator is started before initial state preparation so that its strength is stabilized when the joint evolution begins, maintained throughout the 12-qubit evolution, and accompanied by a Z-bias compensation for the measurement-induced Stark shift. Γm/2π is set to calibrated values including 0, 5.921, 11.195, and 18.134 MHz. At each evolution time, the qubit populations <n_i> are obtained by simultaneous projective readout of the 12 active sites. The spatial-geometric scope is the complete 12-site interferometer, with population dynamics compared along both arms and at Q15 over the full 0–200 ns evolution window.

continuous_measurement_quantum_zeno_refl.description: Whether continuous which-way monitoring of Q2 produced measurement-induced reflection of the propagating microwave photon in the 12-qubit interferometer dynamics.

dominant_transport_path_at_strong_contin.description: Dominant interferometer arm carrying the propagating excitation under the strongest continuous which-way measurement condition.

zeno_onset_comparison_dephasing_rate_mhz.description: Characteristic dephasing-rate scale identified for the onset of Zeno-dominated behavior by comparison with the Q0–Q2 hopping rate.

experiment_description: Two-qubit tomography experiment on the two arms of the continuously monitored 12-qubit superconducting-qubit Mach–Zehnder interferometer, configured to quantify quantum-information leakage and its modification by quantum-Zeno backaction. The active device and interferometer geometry are the 12-site Q0-to-Q15 Mach–Zehnder network on the 4×4 transmon processor: path 1 contains Q1, Q4, Q5, Q7, and Q13, while path 2 contains Q2, Q8, Q10, Q11, and Q14. The monitored which-way site is Q2. Initial-state post-selection, Q0 excitation, tuning of all interferometer qubits to 5.82 GHz, and continuous Q2 dispersive measurement are performed as in the 12-qubit population-dynamics experiment. The calibrated continuous measurement-induced dephasing Γm/2π is swept over the plotted range from 0 to about 24 MHz. Two-qubit tomography is performed on Q4 and Q8, one qubit on each arm downstream of the monitored entrance region, at the fixed evolution time corresponding to the maximum Q4–Q8 concurrence in the absence of the which-way measurement. From the reconstructed rho_Q4Q8, concurrence CQ4Q8 is computed using the Wootters definition. The single-excitation subspace density matrix is formed with P = |10><10| + |01><01| as rho_s = P rho_Q4Q8 P / Tr(P rho_Q4Q8), with purity Ps = Tr(rho_s^2) and von Neumann entropy Ss = -Tr(rho_s log2 rho_s). The spatial-geometric scope is the paired downstream arm sites Q4 and Q8, sampled as a function of the continuously monitored Q2 measurement strength.
